title: New York Slave Revolt of 1712
description: Enslaved Africans and Indigenous people in New York City stage an armed revolt against colonial rule, met with brutal reprisals and harsher slave codes.

title: Nanny of the Maroons Leads Resistance
description: Nanny, a Jamaican Maroon leader, helps coordinate resistance to British colonial forces and protects autonomous communities.

title: Stono Rebellion
description: The largest slave uprising in the British mainland colonies erupts in South Carolina, prompting the strictest slave codes yet enacted.

title: Tacky's War
description: Enslaved Akan people in Jamaica rise up under Tacky, the largest revolt in the British Caribbean before the Haitian Revolution.

title: Phillis Wheatley Publishes Poetry
description: Phillis Wheatley becomes one of the first published African American poets, challenging ideas about race, intellect, and authorship.

title: Haitian Revolution Begins
description: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise up and begin the only successful slave revolution in history, leading to Haiti's independence.

title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
description: Mary Wollstonecraft publishes one of the first works of feminist philosophy, arguing women are rational beings deserving education and equality.
wikiLink: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

title: American School for the Deaf Opens
description: The first permanent school for deaf students in the U.S. opens in Hartford, founding American Sign Language in the process.

title: Mary Prince Testifies About Slavery
description: The History of Mary Prince becomes a major first-person account of slavery by a Black woman in the British Caribbean.

title: Amistad Rebellion
description: Captive Mende people seize the schooner La Amistad off Cuba, and their fight for freedom reaches the U.S. Supreme Court.

title: Frederick Douglass Launches The North Star
description: Douglass creates an abolitionist newspaper amplifying anti-slavery writing and Black political thought.

title: Seneca Falls Convention
description: The first women's rights convention drafts a Declaration of Sentiments demanding equal rights, including the vote.

title: Sojourner Truth Delivers Ain't I a Woman?
description: Sojourner Truth links abolition and women's rights, exposing how race and gender oppression intersect.

title: Harriet Tubman Leads Rescue Missions
description: Tubman leads intelligence and liberation missions during the US Civil War, including the Combahee Ferry Raid.

title: First Native American Woman Doctor Licensed in US
description: Susan La Flesche Picotte earns her medical degree and serves Native communities with a focus on public health.

title: Ida B. Wells Publishes Anti-Lynching Investigations
description: Wells documents racial terror in investigative journalism, shaping global anti-lynching activism.

title: New Zealand Grants Women the Vote
description: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to let women vote, following a decades-long suffrage campaign.

title: Uprising of the 20,000
description: Mostly young immigrant women garment workers strike against sweatshop conditions in New York, winning the largest women's strike to date.

title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
description: 146 workers, mostly immigrant women, die in a locked-door factory fire, galvanizing the movement for workplace safety laws.

title: 19th Amendment Ratified
description: The U.S. Constitution finally prohibits denying the vote on the basis of sex, though many women of color remain excluded for decades.
wikiLink: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: Yuri Kochiyama Born; Future Cross-Movement Organizer
description: Kochiyama later becomes a key organizer connecting Japanese American redress, Black liberation, and anti-imperialist struggles.

title: Society for Human Rights Founded
description: Henry Gerber founds the first gay rights organization in the United States in Chicago, publishing the country's first gay-interest newsletter.

title: Zora Neale Hurston's Anthropological Work Gains Reach
description: Hurston's fieldwork and writing preserve Black folklore traditions often dismissed by mainstream scholarship.

title: Mendez v. Westminster Challenges School Segregation
description: Mexican American families in California win a key desegregation case that influences later civil rights litigation.

title: Mattachine Society Founded
description: Harry Hay and others found the Mattachine Society, an early U.S. homophile organization that challenged police harassment and invisibility.

title: Henrietta Lacks' Cells Become HeLa
description: Cells taken from Henrietta Lacks without her knowledge become the first immortal human cell line, powering decades of medicine while her family went uncompensated.

title: Claudette Colvin Refuses to Give Up Her Seat
description: Months before the more widely known boycott moment, Claudette Colvin's resistance becomes part of legal strategy against bus segregation.

title: Montgomery Bus Boycott
description: After Rosa Parks is arrested, Black residents of Montgomery sustain a year-long bus boycott that ends segregated seating.

title: Greensboro Sit-Ins
description: Four Black college students refuse to leave a Woolworth lunch counter, igniting sit-ins that spread across the segregated South.

title: Dolores Huerta Co-Founds United Farm Workers
description: Huerta helps organize farmworkers for labor rights, better pay, and safer working conditions.

title: Ed Roberts Enters UC Berkeley
description: Ed Roberts becomes the first student with severe disabilities admitted to UC Berkeley, launching the independent living movement.

title: Equal Pay Act Signed
description: The U.S. bans wage discrimination on the basis of sex, a landmark step in the fight for pay equity.

title: Nina Simone Releases Mississippi Goddam
description: Nina Simone turns performance into protest, using music to confront racist violence in the US.

title: Voting Rights Act Signed
description: Federal law finally outlaws literacy tests and other barriers that had kept Black Americans from the ballot for a century.

title: Delano Grape Strike Begins
description: Filipino and Mexican farmworkers strike in Delano, California, building a national grape boycott and the United Farm Workers.

title: Black Panther Party Founded
description: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale found the Black Panther Party in Oakland, pairing self-defense with free breakfast, health, and education programs.

title: American Indian Movement Founded
description: AIM is founded to address police brutality, treaty rights, sovereignty, and conditions in Native communities.

title: Stonewall Uprising
description: Patrons of the Stonewall Inn resist a police raid in Greenwich Village, igniting the modern LGBTQ+ liberation movement.

title: Title IX Signed
description: The U.S. outlaws sex discrimination in education, transforming access to sports, scholarships, and campuses for women.

title: Trail of Broken Treaties
description: The American Indian Movement's cross-country caravan occupies the BIA headquarters in Washington to protest broken treaties.

title: Homosexuality Removed from DSM
description: The American Psychiatric Association declassifies homosexuality as a mental illness after years of activism inside and outside the profession.

title: Wounded Knee Occupation
description: Oglala Lakota and AIM activists occupy Wounded Knee for 71 days, forcing national attention on treaty rights.

title: The Combahee River Collective Statement
description: Black feminist organizers articulate an intersectional political framework centered on those most marginalized.

title: Section 504 Sit-Ins
description: Disabled activists occupy federal buildings for weeks to force enforcement of disability rights law, the longest sit-in at a federal site.

title: Harvey Milk Elected in San Francisco
description: Harvey Milk becomes one of the first openly gay elected officials in the U.S., only to be assassinated months later.

title: Rigoberta Menchu's Testimonio Goes Global
description: The life narrative of Rigoberta Menchu highlights Indigenous rights struggles in Guatemala for international audiences.

title: Dr. Flossie Wong-Staal Helps Map HIV
description: Virologist Flossie Wong-Staal's work on HIV genetics advances understanding and testing in the AIDS crisis.

title: Disability Rights Movement Wins ADA
description: Activists secure the Americans with Disabilities Act, reshaping access and anti-discrimination law.

title: Americans with Disabilities Act Signed
description: The U.S. outlaws discrimination against disabled people in employment, public spaces, and services, a model adopted worldwide.

title: NAGPRA Signed
description: The U.S. requires museums to return Indigenous remains and sacred objects, beginning the repatriation of stolen heritage.
wikiLink: Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act

title: Lawrence v. Texas
description: The U.S. Supreme Court strikes down sodomy laws, ruling that intimate same-sex conduct is protected by the Constitution.

title: Wangari Maathai Wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: Maathai is recognized for linking environmental restoration, women's leadership, and democratic rights in Kenya.

title: Black Lives Matter Founded
description: Three Black women found Black Lives Matter after the acquittal of Trayvon Martin's killer, growing into a global movement.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges
description: The U.S. Supreme Court legalizes same-sex marriage nationwide, capping a generation of advocacy.

title: Standing Rock Water Protectors
description: The Standing Rock Sioux and allies camp at the confluence of the Missouri and Cannonball rivers to stop the Dakota Access Pipeline.

title: Tarana Burke's Me Too Movement Expands
description: Tarana Burke's long-running survivor-centered framework reaches global scale and reshapes discussions of accountability.

title: Global George Floyd Protests
description: The killing of George Floyd sparks the largest protest movement in U.S. history and a worldwide reckoning on policing and race.

title: Land Back and Language Revitalization Campaigns Grow
description: Indigenous-led movements around land stewardship and language renewal gain broader institutional support.

title: UAW Stand-Up Strike Wins Record Contracts
description: The United Auto Workers' six-week stand-up strike against the Big Three automakers wins record wage and benefit gains.

title: European Accessibility Act Takes Effect
description: EU-wide accessibility rules for everyday products and services become enforceable, extending rights beyond public buildings.
